milestones.title: M0 Foundations
milestones.description: Repo, build, CI, docs baseline. The skeleton compiles and runs in the simulator.

milestones.title: M1 Protocol discovery
milestones.description: The FxChip BLE's advertising, GATT and packet format are known and documented from captures.

milestones.description: The watch reliably connects to a real chip and receives every crossing.

milestones.title: M3 Splits & FIT
milestones.description: Crossings become splits/reps with correct µs times and land in the FIT file and Garmin Connect.

milestones.title: M4 Usable v0.1

milestones.title: M5 Beyond v0.1

issues.title: Build the skeleton with the Connect IQ SDK and fix compile errors
issues.requirement: The project as committed must compile with the current Connect IQ SDK for every product listed in manifest.xml, with type checking at level 1, and launch in the simulator without a runtime crash on the initial view.
acceptance: `monkeyc -f monkey.jungle -d fr255 -l 1 -o bin/freelap.prg -y <key>` exits 0 with no errors
The same command succeeds for at least one API 3.1 device (e.g. fr245) and one API 5.x device (e.g. fr965)
App launches in the simulator, shows the 'Scanning for chip…' state, and START creates a session without exception
Any API-level workaround needed for 3.1 devices is commented in the code and listed in docs/DESIGN.md §9
issues.notes: Known risk areas from review: module-level `var` in FreelapProtocol, ByteArray.addAll return, Long arithmetic from decodeNumber, Menu2 on older devices.

issues.title: Add a launcher icon and per-device resource overrides
issues.requirement: The app has a launcher icon in the sizes the target devices need and the main view renders legibly on round 208px, 240px, 260px, 280px and 416px displays.
acceptance: resources/drawables/launcher_icon.png exists; the launcher shows it on fr245, fr255 and fr965 simulators
MainView text does not clip or overlap on any of the listed resolutions (screenshots attached to the PR)
Fonts are chosen via resource overrides where needed rather than hard-coded sizes

issues.title: CI: validate resources and tooling on every push; document the SDK constraint
issues.requirement: GitHub Actions validates everything that can be validated without the Garmin SDK (XML resources, Python tools, issues.json) and the README explains why monkeyc is not run in CI and how to add it via a self-hosted runner.
acceptance: .github/workflows/lint.yml passes on main
A malformed strings.xml or issues.json fails the workflow
README 'Build' section links to the CI note

issues.title: Spike: enumerate the FxChip BLE's advertising data and GATT table
issues.requirement: We know exactly how to recognise and subscribe to the chip: advertised name, service UUIDs, manufacturer data (company id + bytes), every service/characteristic UUID with its properties (read/write/notify/indicate), and the CCCD handles.
acceptance: captures/<date>/gatt.md lists every service and characteristic with UUID, properties and (if readable) initial value, taken with nRF Connect or equivalent
Advertising payload is recorded raw (hex) plus decoded fields; name prefix and service UUID are confirmed
Whether the chip advertises while MyFreelap is *not* connected, and whether it accepts a second central while MyFreelap *is* connected, are both answered explicitly
FreelapProtocol.mc constants SERVICE_UUID_STR / NOTIFY_UUID_STR / COMMAND_UUID_STR / NAME_PREFIXES are updated and the HYPOTHESIS markers on them removed
issues.notes: Blocks #M1 packet-format spike and all of M2. See docs/REVERSE-ENGINEERING.md 'Kit'.

issues.title: Spike: capture MyFreelap ↔ chip traffic for the scripted run set
issues.requirement: A complete, annotated capture exists for runs A–G in docs/REVERSE-ENGINEERING.md, taken with Android HCI snoop or an nRF sniffer, with the MyFreelap-displayed values and wall-clock notes for each run.
acceptance: captures/<date>/cap.tsv (tshark export with frame.time_epoch, btatt.handle, btatt.value) committed
captures/<date>/runs.md records, per run, transmitters crossed, MyFreelap split values, and any observation (e.g. 'no packet until FINISH')
Any ATT writes the app performs after connecting (handshake) are listed with hex payloads and the characteristic they target
Capture includes at least one rep with ≥3 crossings and at least one fragmented (>20 byte) notification if the chip produces them

issues.title: Decode the crossing packet format from captures
issues.requirement: The packet layout is fully specified: framing/sync, length or count field, per-crossing record stride, timestamp offset/width/endianness/unit, transmitter-code field and its values for START/LAP/FINISH, chip identifier, checksum (if any), and fragmentation rules.
acceptance: docs/PROTOCOL.md documents the layout with a byte-by-byte table and at least two worked examples from real packets
`tools/decode_capture.py captures/<date>/cap.tsv <times>` locates every MyFreelap split value in the capture at the documented offsets
Timestamp unit is stated with evidence (which run/values proved it) and whether it is relative to START or absolute chip uptime
Whether the chip notifies per crossing or bursts at FINISH is stated and FreelapProtocol.STREAMING set accordingly
Open questions that captures could not answer are listed at the end of docs/PROTOCOL.md

issues.title: Implement the real FreelapProtocol decoder with unit-test vectors
issues.requirement: FreelapProtocol.feed() decodes real packets (including reassembly of fragmented notifications and rejection of malformed input) into Crossing objects with time in microseconds and TxCode, and the decoder is covered by test vectors taken from captures.
acceptance: All HYPOTHESIS comments in FreelapProtocol.mc are removed or replaced by references to docs/PROTOCOL.md
A Connect IQ unit test (Toybox.Test, `monkeyc --unit-test`) or a Python reference decoder in tools/ reproduces every crossing in captures/<date>/runs.md from cap.tsv byte-for-byte
Garbage input (wrong sync, truncated packet, oversized count) returns null and leaves the reassembly buffer reset
TICK_US is set from evidence; converting a packet's timestamp yields the MyFreelap-displayed value to within display rounding

issues.title: Ask Freelap for protocol documentation / SDK
issues.requirement: Freelap has been asked, in writing, whether they will share the FxChip BLE GATT/packet specification for a Garmin integration, and their answer (including any NDA terms) is recorded.
acceptance: Email sent to Freelap SA and/or Freelap USA; date and contact recorded in this issue
Reply (or 30 days of silence) recorded; if a spec is received under NDA, the repo notes which parts of FreelapProtocol.mc may not be published

issues.title: Reliable scan → pair → subscribe against the real chip
issues.requirement: On launch the app finds the chip within 10 s when it is advertising within ~5 m, pairs, enables notifications (and sends any handshake writes), and reaches BleState.SUBSCRIBED without user interaction.
acceptance: 10 consecutive cold launches on a real watch reach 'Chip OK' within 10 s of the chip advertising (log the times in the PR)
onProfileRegister reports STATUS_SUCCESS; a failure is surfaced on screen rather than silently retried
A chip that is present but not advertising (asleep) results in the SCANNING state persisting, not an error
Handshake writes (if the protocol needs them) are sent in order and each waits for its onCharacteristicWrite before the next

issues.title: Reconnect after link loss without losing crossings already received
issues.requirement: If the BLE link drops mid-session (range, chip reset), the app returns to scanning with exponential backoff and re-subscribes automatically; the session keeps recording; crossings decoded before the drop are intact and the reassembly buffer is reset so a partial packet cannot corrupt the next one.
acceptance: Walk the chip out of range for 30 s and back: the app shows a non-connected state within 5 s of the drop and returns to 'Chip OK' within 20 s of the chip being back in range, with no user input
After 5 failed retries the app shows 'No chip' and offers a manual rescan (START on the connect screen or a menu item) instead of retrying forever
A rep completed after reconnection is written to the FIT file with the correct rep number (continues from before the drop)

issues.title: Remember the last chip and prefer it when several are advertising
issues.requirement: The app stores the identity of the last chip it connected to and, when multiple Freelap chips are in range (a group session), connects to that one; the user can forget it and pick another from a list.
acceptance: With two chips advertising, the app reconnects to the previously used chip 10/10 times
A 'Choose chip' menu lists all matching scan results with name and RSSI and lets the user pick one; the choice is persisted
Identity is stored as the most stable identifier the chip exposes (name + address hash or chip id from advertising), documented in DESIGN.md §6

issues.title: Capture mode: on-watch raw packet logger
issues.requirement: With the captureMode setting on, the watch shows the last raw notification (hex) and packet count on screen and keeps a rolling log of the last N packets with System.getTimer() arrival stamps in Application.Storage, flushed at app exit, retrievable via the simulator or a debug menu.
acceptance: Rolling log holds at least 60 packets without exceeding Storage value limits on an API 3.1 device
No flash write happens per packet (verified by code review); the log is written on stop()/save()
A debug menu item 'Dump capture' prints the log to the CIQ console when run in the simulator, in the same TSV shape tools/decode_capture.py reads

issues.title: Course model: parse, validate and match crossings to transmitters
issues.requirement: A course string (e.g. `S:0;L:30;L:60;F:100`) is parsed into an ordered transmitter list with cumulative distances; invalid strings are rejected with a message; crossings are matched to course indices by code sequence with index-order fallback, and mismatches are flagged rather than guessed.
acceptance: Unit tests cover: valid 2-, 3- and 5-transmitter courses; non-monotonic distances (rejected); missing FINISH (accepted, flagged as open-ended); unknown code letter (rejected); empty string (falls back to default and warns)
A rep with an extra crossing (more than the course has) yields txIndex = -1 for the extra and RepStatus.UNMATCHED
A rep that ends before FINISH (manual lap or chip timeout) yields RepStatus.PARTIAL with distance = last matched transmitter's distance
Course parse errors are shown on the watch when settings change (onSettingsChanged), not only in the log

issues.title: Split engine: derive split/cumulative time (µs), distance, velocity, speed and pace
issues.requirement: For each crossing the engine produces split_time_us, cum_time_us (both integer microseconds, no rounding), split and cumulative distance from the course, velocity in m/s, speed in km/h and pace in s/km, plus rep totals (time, distance, average and peak velocity, split count, status).
acceptance: Unit tests with hand-computed expectations for a 30/30/40 m course at 4.120 s / 7.480 s / 11.930 s: split_us = 4120000, 3360000, 4450000; velocities 7.282, 8.929, 8.989 m/s (±0.001); pace 137.3 s/km for split 1 (±0.1)
Chip timestamps that are absolute uptime (Long) do not overflow; a rep starting at uptime > 2^31 µs produces correct relative times
A split with zero distance or zero time produces velocity/speed/pace = 0 and no exception
Rep totals: best rep is tracked only over RepStatus.OK reps; total distance sums all reps

issues.title: Estimated wall-clock placement of crossings (BLE latency model)
issues.requirement: Each crossing gets an estimated time in ms since session start, derived from the packet arrival time minus a configurable BLE latency and the chip's relative times, and this estimate is clearly labelled as an estimate everywhere it is shown or stored.
acceptance: bleLatencyMs setting is applied; changing it changes fl_est_ms by exactly the delta
For a burst at FINISH, START's estimate = FINISH estimate − rep_time; intermediate crossings are placed proportionally
Ten timed trials against a phone stopwatch on a real chip give a median absolute error < 300 ms with the default latency; the measured latency is recorded in docs/DESIGN.md §3
Estimates are never negative (clamped to 0 with a flag if the packet arrives before session start)

issues.title: FIT: record-level developer fields for every split
issues.requirement: Every split is written to the FIT file as the record-level developer fields defined in DESIGN.md §5 (ids 0–9), one split per record, in order, with uint32 microsecond fields preserved exactly, and the fields cleared (or held, per setting) on the following record.
acceptance: FitCSVTool (FIT SDK) on a session file shows field_description messages for all 10 record fields with the documented names, types and units
A rep with 4 crossings produces exactly 4 consecutive records carrying fl_rep = N and fl_tx_idx 0..3, with fl_split_us equal to the engine's values byte-for-byte
With clearAfterWrite = true the record after the last split has fl_split_us = 0 and fl_tx_idx = 255; with false it repeats the last values
Garmin Connect shows fl_velocity and fl_split_us as chartable developer fields on the activity
Splits queued when the session is paused are written when it resumes, not dropped

issues.title: FIT: one Garmin lap per Freelap rep with lap-level summary fields
issues.requirement: Each completed rep closes a Garmin lap carrying fl_rep_time_us, fl_rep_dist_m, fl_rep_avg_vel, fl_rep_peak_vel, fl_rep_splits and fl_rep_status, and the lap is closed only after all of the rep's split records have been written.
acceptance: A session with 5 reps produces 5 lap messages (plus the trailing partial lap Garmin adds) each with all six developer fields populated — verified with FitCSVTool
Lap developer fields survive on API 3.1 and 5.x devices (the known forum bug is worked around by the deferred addLap); test evidence from both attached
Garmin Connect's Laps table shows the rep time and distance columns
The lapPerCrossing setting, when on, produces one lap per crossing instead, with lap fields populated from the split

issues.title: FIT: session summary fields and correct save/discard behaviour
issues.requirement: On save the session message carries fl_reps, fl_best_rep_us, fl_total_dist_m and fl_chip_id; queued splits and a pending lap are flushed before save; discard leaves no partial FIT file; exiting the app with an unsaved session prompts rather than silently discarding.
acceptance: FitCSVTool shows the four session fields with correct values for a 3-rep test session
Save immediately after a FINISH burst still contains all of that rep's records and its lap
Discard from the menu results in no new activity in Garmin Connect after sync
Pressing BACK to exit with an active session shows the Save/Discard menu; onStop never discards a session that has been saved
Sport/sub-sport are Running / Track and the activity is classified as a track run in Garmin Connect

issues.title: Store the full split log on the watch and expose it for export
issues.requirement: Independently of the FIT file, every split of the last session is stored in Application.Storage as compact arrays with full µs precision and can be retrieved (simulator console dump, or a future companion app) as CSV.
acceptance: lastSessionSplits survives app restart and contains one row per split with rep, tx index, code, cum µs, split µs, distances, velocity and est ms
Storage size stays below the per-value limit for a session of 40 reps × 5 splits (chunk if necessary)
tools/splits_to_csv.py converts a dumped log into CSV with a header row

issues.title: Activity screen: live split readout, rep counter, chip status
issues.requirement: While recording, the main screen shows chip connection state, the latest split's velocity (large), its time/distance/pace (small), rep count and last rep time, and a PAUSED indicator; the screen updates within 200 ms of a burst arriving.
acceptance: Layout matches the wireframe in DESIGN.md §7 on 240px and 416px round displays (screenshots in PR)
Velocity shown to 2 decimals in m/s; split time to 1/100 s; pace as m:ss/km
Chip status colours: green subscribed, yellow scanning/pairing, red none
Screen remains readable with the backlight off on MIP displays (no thin grey text)

issues.title: Rep summary overlay after each FINISH
issues.requirement: When a rep completes, a summary view shows a table of the rep's splits (transmitter, split time, velocity) and the rep total for 5 s or until dismissed, then returns to the activity screen without interfering with recording.
acceptance: Overlay appears within 500 ms of onRepComplete and auto-dismisses after 5 s; any key dismisses it early
Up to 6 splits fit on a 240px display; more scroll
Recording, BLE reception and the 1 Hz FIT tick continue while the overlay is shown (a second rep arriving during the overlay is not lost)

issues.title: On-watch course selection and Quick course
issues.requirement: Before starting, the user can pick one of the configured courses or a Quick course (START + FINISH at a distance dialled on the watch, 10–400 m in 5 m steps) without needing the phone.
acceptance: Menu lists configured courses by name with total distance; selecting one sets activeCourse and persists
Quick course picker sets a two-transmitter course and shows the chosen distance on the activity screen
Changing course mid-session is refused with a message (course applies to the whole session)

issues.title: Settings via Garmin Connect / Express: courses, latency, flags
issues.requirement: All settings in resources/settings are editable from the Garmin Connect app, validated on onSettingsChanged, and applied without restarting the app where possible.
acceptance: Editing course2 in Garmin Connect and syncing updates the course list on the watch within one sync, with parse errors shown on the watch
bleLatencyMs, clearAfterWrite, lapPerCrossing, captureMode take effect for the next session without relaunch
Up to 8 courses are supported (extend properties.xml / settings.xml)

issues.title: Manual controls: pause/resume, manual rep end, save/discard
issues.requirement: START toggles pause/resume; BACK/LAP while recording ends the current rep manually (for courses without a FINISH transmitter or a missed crossing); BACK while paused opens Save/Discard; touch devices get equivalent on-screen controls.
acceptance: Manual rep end on a rep with 2 matched crossings writes a lap with RepStatus.PARTIAL
Manual rep end with no crossings pending is a no-op with a short 'No splits' toast
Pause stops the FIT timer; Garmin's elapsed vs timer time differ accordingly in Connect
On a touch-only device (venu) all three actions are reachable

issues.title: Field validation: 20 reps on a real track against MyFreelap
issues.requirement: A full session on a real course (≥3 transmitters, ≥20 reps, phone app running in parallel if the chip allows, otherwise alternating) demonstrates that every split recorded by the watch matches MyFreelap to the chip's resolution and no rep is lost.
acceptance: Side-by-side table of watch (from FIT via FitCSVTool) vs MyFreelap for every split, committed under captures/<date>/validation.md
0 missing reps, 0 extra reps; all split times equal within the chip's display resolution
Garmin Connect activity screenshot showing laps and at least one developer-field chart
Battery drain of the watch over the session recorded

issues.title: Robustness: memory and watchdog on API 3.1 devices
issues.requirement: The app stays within the memory budget of the smallest supported device across a 2-hour session with 60 reps and does not trigger watchdog resets on packet bursts.
acceptance: Simulator memory view on fr245 shows peak usage < 80% of the app limit after a scripted 60-rep replay via tools/fake_chip.py
No 'Watchdog Tripped' in a 60-rep replay; onCharacteristicChanged does no Storage writes and no string building beyond capture mode
The split log and capture buffer are bounded (documented limits)

issues.title: Fake chip: replay real captures and multi-fragment bursts
issues.requirement: tools/fake_chip.py can replay a captured session (cap.tsv) with original inter-packet timing, and generate synthetic multi-rep sessions in the real packet format, so the pipeline can be regression-tested without transmitters.
acceptance: `fake_chip.py --replay captures/<date>/cap.tsv` reproduces the notifications with timing within ±20 ms
`fake_chip.py --synthetic --reps 60 --course S:0;L:30;L:60;F:100` runs unattended and the watch records 60 laps
Script works on Linux/BlueZ; macOS limitation documented

issues.title: Multi-athlete: Freelap Relay Coach BLE / several chips
issues.requirement: The app can receive crossings tagged with a chip id (from a Relay Coach BLE or by connecting to several chips) and keeps separate rep state per chip, writing the chip id with every split.
acceptance: Design note in DESIGN.md §6 updated with the chosen approach and its BLE profile budget (max 3 profiles)
Two chips produce interleaved reps with correct per-chip rep numbering and fl_chip_id on each record
UI shows which chip the latest split belongs to

issues.title: CSV / Intervals.icu export path for splits
issues.requirement: Splits recorded by the watch can be exported as CSV and pushed to a training platform (Intervals.icu activity intervals or custom fields) from a desktop tool that reads the FIT developer fields.
acceptance: tools/fit_splits.py reads a FIT file and prints one CSV row per split with µs precision using the FIT SDK or fitdecode
Documented mapping from fl_* fields to the target platform's fields
Round-trip test: watch FIT → CSV matches the on-watch split log exactly

issues.title: Connect IQ store readiness
issues.requirement: The app meets Connect IQ store submission requirements: unique app id, permissions justified, screenshots, description, privacy statement (no data leaves the watch), and a support link.
acceptance: manifest.xml id regenerated; product list reviewed against tested devices
Store listing text and 5 screenshots in docs/store/
Trademark note: 'Freelap' is Freelap SA's mark; listing states the app is unofficial
